topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture themes, connects them to practical coursework, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumor virology, oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace the history of tumor virology, the discovery of transduced cellular proto-oncogenes, and the laboratory assays used to test cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification, regulation, and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the functional definitions of cancer mutations, the regulation of cell cycle checkpoints, and the effects of allele dosage and mutation type on cellular phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the various defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitosis that produce sequence and chromosomal instability alongside their downstream cellular consequences.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis, hereditary predispositions, and tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: They explore how the stepwise acquisition and inheritance of cancer mutations drive tumor development and how genetic stability influences tumor evolution and therapy response.

topics.label: Conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a review of the learning outcomes, recommended reading, and a preview of the upcoming session.
